hypotheses.justification: The statement stays true without `ha`. If a ≤ 2^N, the original proof applies, using `hb` or the case split on b. If a > 2^N, then H N a ≥ H N (2^N) = 2^N by `H_mono` and `H_full`. So max (H N a) b ≥ 2^N, and max (H N b) a ≥ a > 2^N. The RHS is therefore > 2^(N+1). The LHS satisfies H (N+1) (a+b) ≤ 2^(N+1) by `H_le_cube`, so the inequality holds. The junk case is harmless because `simplicialInitSeg` is `rank x < k`, which is the whole cube for large k. The proof becomes a case split on a ≤ 2^N, using the existing argument in one branch and this estimate in the other. The same applies to `hb`, so each hypothesis can be dropped on its own. Both can also be dropped together, because the cases a > 2^N, b > 2^N, and both ≤ 2^N are each covered.

The statement stays true without `hb`. If b ≤ 2^N, use the original proof. If b > 2^N, then H N b ≥ H N (2^N) = 2^N by `H_mono` and `H_full`. So max (H N b) a ≥ 2^N, and max (H N a) b ≥ b > 2^N. The RHS is therefore > 2^(N+1), while the LHS is ≤ 2^(N+1) by `H_le_cube`. The proof is a case split on b ≤ 2^N, using the existing argument in one branch and this bound in the other. This is symmetric to `ha`. Both hypotheses can be dropped together by splitting on whether a or b exceeds 2^N.
